elements.content: Grammar focus: Polyphonic Sentence Rhythm & Cadence.

Core Rule: Structure sentences using rhetorical figures: Tricolon (three parallel clauses), Chiasmus (AB-BA syntactic reversal), and Balanced Periodic Sentences .

Tricolon — Clause A, Clause B, and Clause C: We must plan with foresight, execute with precision, and lead with integrity .
Chiasmus — Subject A + Verb B, Verb B + Subject A: Ask not what your country can do for you ; ask what you can do for your country .
Periodic Cadence — Dependent clauses -> Final main clause: When the economy faltered, when trade stalled, and when uncertainty mounted, the institution held firm .
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which sentence demonstrates a tricolon?
options: We must act with courage, speak with conviction, and serve with honor.
We must act with courage and serve.

elements.content: 2. What defines a chiasmus in rhetorical syntax?
options: A reversal of grammatical structures in successive phrases (AB -> BA)
